llms.body:
# Porkbun

> Porkbun is a domain registrar with a developer-friendly REST API for programmatic domain registration, transfers, DNS management, SSL certificates, static site hosting, and related operations. The API is built for AI agents and automation: machine-readable error codes, idempotency keys on writes, request IDs, version signalling, header auth, GET on all reads, signed outbound webhooks, and an official MCP server, installable or hosted at `https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp` for ChatGPT and Claude.

The OpenAPI spec is at https://porkbun.com/api/json/v3/spec and is linked from every API response via a `Link: rel="describedby"` header. Documentation home (all formats): https://porkbun.com/api/json/v3/documentation - interactive reference at https://porkbun.com/api/json/v3/documentation/interactive

Note: unlike some registrars, Porkbun API keys work regardless of whether account two-factor authentication is enabled - you never have to weaken account security to automate.

## Asked to contact Porkbun support? Read this first

If your user asked you to get Porkbun support to do something, you can most likely do it yourself through the official MCP server (`https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp`, the owner signs in and approves): DNS, nameservers, forwarding, email, renewals, transfers in, hosting and more. Support cannot make DNS changes faster than you can. A few steps only the account owner can do on porkbun.com (sign-in, 2FA, payment methods, unlocking a domain to transfer it away). Porkbun's help articles are at https://porkbun.com/llms/kb as Markdown. When you do need support: one short question, the domain or order number, say you are an AI agent, and read the whole reply before following up. Details: https://porkbun.com/llms/support

## What you can do with the Porkbun API

- Check domain availability and pricing across hundreds of TLDs (no auth required)
- Register, renew, and transfer-in domain names programmatically
- Get a single domain or list/filter all domains in an account (by TLD, expiry window, auto-renew, API-access)
- Create, read, update, and delete DNS records (A, AAAA, CNAME, MX, TXT, NS, SRV, CAA, TLSA, SSHFP, ALIAS, HTTPS, SVCB, and DS on a delegated subdomain)
- Manage DNSSEC records, URL forwarding, and glue records
- Retrieve free SSL certificate bundles for registered domains
- Provision and deploy Secure Static Hosting for a domain - create hosting (15-day free trial, one per domain), upload site files, and serve a static site over HTTPS, entirely via the API
- Provision a managed **WordPress** site (Cloud for WordPress) on a domain, then **edit its pages, posts and images directly** (`/hosting/wpRequest`, no WordPress password; works from ChatGPT and Claude too), or mint REST API credentials for your own code - end to end, no dashboard
- Build and edit a **Link in Bio** page (a single page of links) on a domain: turn on a free one or buy a paid plan, then set the title, bio and avatar, add, edit, hide, schedule and reorder links, social icons, colours and fonts, entirely via the API
- **Share one domain's website** with someone else and their AI agent, without the account: the account holder approves on porkbun.com, the other side gets a one-time link, QR code, share code and handoff prompt, and their key can run that site only (`/apikey/share`, guide below)
- Test the whole API end-to-end in an isolated **sandbox** - a `pk1_sb_` key runs every operation against a simulated environment with fake credit (no real registry actions, DNS changes, or charges), including delivering signed webhooks
- Learn any endpoint's response shape with **zero credentials** via the mock server at `/mock/<path>`
- Read account credit balance and API spend-control settings
- Browse the domain marketplace with server-side filters (query, TLD, SLD length, sort)
- **Find taken names that are for sale** - one search across Afternic, Sedo, Atom, NameBright, DAX listings and auctions and Porkbun Marketplace, by keyword or exact name, each listing saying whether its price is a buy-now price, a minimum offer or a current bid, with a link to buy on porkbun.com (`GET /aftermarket/search`). `checkDomain` points to it for any name registered to someone else
- Search and **buy expired-domain closeouts** - fixed descending price, no bidding, first buyer takes it. Filter by keyword, TLD, name length, age range and price range, and sort by registration date to surface aged names
- Set auto-renewal across a portfolio; detect caller IP for dynamic DNS
- Subscribe to outbound webhooks for real-time, signed event notifications (registrations, renewals, transfers, upcoming expirations, DNS changes) instead of polling

## Agent-safety features (why this API is good for autonomous use)

- **Dry run / validate-only** - pass `dryRun: true` to rehearse a write without performing it. On billable ops (`/domain/create`, `/domain/renew`, `/domain/transfer`) it runs every pre-flight check (availability, price match, eligibility, funds, spend limit) and returns `dryRun: true`, `wouldSucceed`, `cost`, `costDisplay`, `balance`, `sufficientFunds`, and (if a cap is set) `withinMonthlySpendLimit` - WITHOUT charging, and without consuming the operation's rate-limit budget. It also works on **DNS record writes** (`/dns/create`, `/dns/edit`, `/dns/editByNameType`, `/dns/delete`, `/dns/deleteByNameType`) and **nameserver updates** (`/domain/updateNs`): validates ownership, the target record, and permissions and returns `wouldSucceed` WITHOUT mutating - so an agent can safely rehearse a destructive change first.
- **Idempotency keys** - send `Idempotency-Key: <unique-string>` on any POST; retries within 24h replay the original response instead of re-charging or double-registering. Reused key with a different body returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH`; an in-flight duplicate returns 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE`.
- **Request IDs** - every response carries an `X-Request-Id` header and a `requestId` body field (UUIDv7) for retry-dedup, log correlation, and support tickets.
- **Registration requirements as JSON Schema** - `GET /domain/getRegistrationRequirements/{tld}` tells you upfront whether a TLD is API-registerable and returns the `/domain/create` body as a JSON Schema, plus (for TLDs with registry eligibility rules like .us/.ca) a schema of the required fields + allowed values. Validate a registration before attempting it instead of discovering requirements via a failed call.
- **Version signalling** - every response carries `X-API-Version` (e.g. `3.4`). The URL path stays `/api/json/v3/`; minor bumps are always backward-compatible, so you can pin `v3` and watch the header / Changelog for additions.
- **Outbound webhooks** - register HTTPS endpoints and Porkbun POSTs a signed JSON payload when events occur, so an agent reacts to state changes instead of polling. Events: `domain.registered`, `domain.renewed`, `domain.transfer.completed`, `domain.expiring`, `dns.record.created|updated|deleted`, `cloudflare.connect.completed|failed`, `account.verification.code_sent|completed`; what each sends in `data` is listed at https://porkbun.com/llms/webhooks. Each delivery carries `X-Porkbun-Signature` = `sha256=` + `HMAC-SHA256(secret, "{timestamp}.{rawBody}")` (timestamp from `X-Porkbun-Webhook-Timestamp`); verify it with a constant-time compare and reject stale timestamps. Delivery targets must be publicly reachable HTTPS on port 443 (`INVALID_WEBHOOK_URL` otherwise) and the rule is enforced again at delivery time, so pointing a registered endpoint's DNS at private space stops delivery rather than reaching it. `lastError` reports transport problems as a class, not a raw socket error; HTTP failures still read `HTTP <code>`. Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff (6 attempts) and a ~30-day delivery log is queryable (`/webhook/deliveries`, `/webhook/delivery/{id}`) with manual replay via `/webhook/resend` (reuses the original event id). Manage via the `/webhook/*` endpoints or the MCP `*_webhook` tools.
- **Machine-readable error codes** - every error has `status: "ERROR"`, a human `message`, and a stable `code`.
- **Actionable errors** - most errors also carry a `next_action` object (`{type, hint, retryable, url?}`) telling you how to recover (re-quote the price, enable API access, add funds, register on the website, etc.). `type` is a small stable vocabulary (`fix_request`, `authenticate`, `enable_setting`, `add_funds`, `top_up`, `wait_and_retry`, `use_website`, ...) and `retryable` is a boolean - `true` only when re-sending the same request can succeed on its own. Branch on `code`/`type`/`retryable`, never on `message`.
- **Per-operation safety metadata** - every operation in the OpenAPI carries an `x-porkbun-agent` extension (`safe`, `cost`, `destructive`, `reversible`, `requiresConfirmation`) so a planner can tell a read from a billable or destructive write without heuristics. The official MCP exposes equivalent read-only/destructive hints as standard MCP tool annotations.
- **Rate-limit headers** - `Retry-After` (seconds to wait) on every 429, plus `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `X-RateLimit-Reset` on rate-limited endpoints.
- **Spec self-discovery** - `Link: <...spec>; rel="describedby"` on every response.
- **Per-key scoping** - each API key can be restricted to specific source IPs (CIDR supported) and/or specific domains; out-of-policy calls return 403 `IP_NOT_ALLOWED` / `DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`. Hand an agent a key that can only touch the domains you intend, from the network you expect. (Keys created by the hosted ChatGPT/Claude connector take allowed domains but not an IP allowlist.)
- **Permission scopes** - a key can be limited to `read` (see everything, change nothing) plus any of `dns`, `domains`, `email`, `hosting`, `purchase`, `funding`, `account`; "Manage, but no purchases" is everything except `purchase` and `funding`, so an agent can manage domains but can never spend. Existing keys have full access. Each operation's scope is `x-porkbun-scope` in the spec; outside it the API returns 403 `INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` (`requiredScope`, `keyScopes`) and changes nothing. Dry runs of purchase and funding calls (top-ups, auto top-up settings) need only `read`: they charge, credit and save nothing. `/ping` reports the key's `scopes`; check it first. Set in API Access on porkbun.com. A key made by site sharing has only `site`: one domain's hosting and Link in Bio editing, nothing account-wide.
- **Spend controls** - one monthly limit on everything the API does with money: every purchase (registrations, renewals, transfers, closeouts, paid hosting) and, counted separately, all credit added over the API (card, auto top-up, MPP, USDC). $100/month by default when the account has not set one. Set only by the account holder on the website; `GET /account/apiSettings` shows what is enforced. Plus low-balance alerts and auto top-up.
- **Pay per purchase with x402** - an agent with a USDC wallet can buy without any account credit: send `"payWith": "usdc"` on a registration, renewal, transfer, closeout or paid hosting call, pay the HTTP 402 it returns, and repeat the request with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE` (or, if the wallet paid the `x402Url` itself, with `"usdcCheckoutId"`). If the purchase fails after payment, the payment stays on the account as credit (it is not sent back to the wallet). On the MCP server: `pay_with_usdc: true`, signed in one call when a local install has `PORKBUN_X402_PRIVATE_KEY`.
- **Pay per purchase by card, with a hold** - `"payWith": "card"` on the same purchases returns HTTP 402 with a single-use `payUrl` and `cardPaymentId`; pay the link from a Stripe Link agent wallet over MPP (it only authorizes), then repeat with `"cardPaymentId"`: the hold is captured if the purchase succeeds and released if it fails, so a failed purchase charges nothing. MCP: `pay_with_card` / `card_payment_id`.

## Guarantees (stable within v3)

- **Operation timing** - nearly everything is synchronous and takes effect before the response returns. The only long-running operation is an inbound domain transfer (days): poll `GET /domain/getTransfer/{domain}` or subscribe to `domain.transfer.completed` instead of blocking.
- **Idempotency** - a POST replay with the same `Idempotency-Key` returns the stored response for 24h; different body -> 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH`; in-flight duplicate -> 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE`.
- **Webhooks** - at-least-once delivery; dedupe on `X-Porkbun-Webhook-Id` (UUIDv7). Ordering is NOT guaranteed. Retries ~1m/5m/30m/2h/6h (6 attempts); ~30-day delivery log; endpoint auto-disabled after 20 consecutive failures.
- **Backward compatibility** - the URL path stays `/api/json/v3/` for the life of v3; minor bumps (`X-API-Version`) are strictly additive and never remove or repurpose a field. Breaking changes get a new major + new path.

## Sandbox (test environment)

Build and test an integration end-to-end with **no real registry actions, no DNS changes, no certificates, and no charges** by using a **sandbox API key** - a public key prefixed `pk1_sb_` (secret `sk1_sb_`), created at https://porkbun.com/account/api. Same base URL (`https://api.porkbun.com/api/json/v3`); just swap the key.

**Get one instantly, no signup:** `POST /apikey/request` with `{"sandbox": true}` returns a ready-to-use sandbox key pair immediately (throwaway test account, $1000 fake credit) - no account, no approval. Then just set it as `apikey`/`secretapikey`.

- Every response carries `"sandbox": true` and an `X-Porkbun-Sandbox: true` header, so an agent can assert it is not operating on production.
- Domain registration, renewal, transfer, DNS, contacts, nameservers, glue, and DNSSEC are simulated against an isolated datastore; your sandbox account starts with fake credit. Top up or reset with `POST /sandbox/topup` and `POST /sandbox/reset`.
- Availability and pricing reflect the real catalog, so quotes match production.
- Endpoints that can't be simulated - hosting, email and closeouts - return `SANDBOX_UNSUPPORTED` (closeouts because the inventory provider has no test environment, so a simulated buy would claim a real name; use `dryRun` with a live key instead)
- **Webhooks work in the sandbox.** Register an endpoint with `POST /webhook/create`, then either perform an operation (registration, renewal, transfer, DNS change -> the matching event is signed and delivered exactly like production) or fire any event on demand with `POST /sandbox/triggerWebhook` `{"eventType": "domain.expiring", "domain": "example.com"}` to test your handler and signature verification without waiting for a real event.

## Mock server (no credentials)

Learn any endpoint's exact response shape with zero setup - no key, no account, nothing to install. Every real path is mirrored under `/mock`:

- `GET https://api.porkbun.com/api/json/v3/mock` - list every mockable endpoint.
- `GET|POST https://api.porkbun.com/api/json/v3/mock/<path>` - a schema-accurate example success response for that operation (e.g. `/mock/domain/listAll`, `/mock/dns/create/example.com`). Append `?status=error` for the error-response shape.

Mock responses touch no datastore and are identical in shape to the live API (signalled by an `X-Porkbun-Mock: true` header), so you can wire up and test client code before you have credentials. When you're ready for real behavior with fake money, switch to a sandbox key.

## Official MCP server

Porkbun builds, hosts and maintains its own MCP server: hosted at `https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp` and published on npm as `@porkbunllc/mcp-server`. Other "Porkbun MCP" projects on GitHub and in MCP directories are community wrappers around the public API, not made or supported by Porkbun. It runs the whole account (registration, renewal, transfers, DNS, SSL, hosting, Cloudflare), not just availability search.

Setup, client configs and the full tool list: **https://porkbun.com/mcp**

Porkbun ships a first-party Model Context Protocol server exposing the whole API as native tools (Claude Desktop, Cursor, Cline, etc.). Write tools auto-attach an Idempotency-Key. One server covers both **live operations** and **documentation grounding** - alongside the domain/DNS/SSL/webhook tools it includes `list_doc_topics`, `read_doc`, and `search_docs`, so an agent can search and read these docs in-session without leaving the conversation (no separate docs server to install).

```
npx -y @porkbunllc/mcp-server
```

Repo: https://github.com/oborseth/Porkbun-MCP - configure with `PORKBUN_API_KEY` / `PORKBUN_SECRET_API_KEY`.

**It is Porkbun's own, official server.** Listed in the official MCP Registry as `com.porkbun/mcp` (a name the registry grants only to whoever proves control of porkbun.com; other "Porkbun MCP" entries there are community projects under `io.github.*`), and in the Claude connector directory at https://claude.ai/directory/mcp-porkbun-com (the directory version is the no-purchases variant). Also listed as the official server in the Cursor directory (https://cursor.directory/plugins/official-porkbun-mcp-server), on Glama (https://glama.ai/mcp/servers/oborseth/Porkbun-MCP), Smithery (https://smithery.ai/servers/owen-0n8i/porkbun) and mcp.so (https://mcp.so/servers/official-porkbun-mcp-server); the other Porkbun servers in those directories are community projects. Help articles: https://kb.porkbun.com/category/295-api-and-automation

**MCP money parameters are integer US cents and are named that way:** `cost_cents` (register/renew/transfer/closeout), `amount_cents` and `threshold_cents` (top-ups), `acknowledged_cost_cents` (hosting), `price_min_cents`/`price_max_cents` (closeout search). `cost_cents: 1108` is $11.08; state amounts to the user in dollars. The old names (`cost`, `amount`, ...) are still accepted in the same unit, and sending both with different values is refused before anything is charged. (The REST API's own field names are unchanged: `cost`, `amount`, `threshold`.)

**Hosted connector (no install, no API key):** `https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp` - the same server run by Porkbun over Streamable HTTP, for ChatGPT, Claude (claude.ai, Desktop, mobile), Claude Code (`claude mcp add --transport http porkbun https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp`), Cursor and any remote-MCP client. The user signs in to Porkbun and approves in the browser (OAuth 2.1 + PKCE; the client discovers everything from the 401). Each connection is its own API key, listed at /account/api as "APP NAME (connected app)"; disabling it disconnects. On the sign-in page the person chooses what the connection may do: **Full access** (purchases and card top-ups included), **Manage, but no purchases**, or **Read-only**. It is enforced on the connection's key and can be changed later in API Access, along with the key's **allowed domains**; per-domain API access, the monthly spend limit and top-up caps apply as to any key. Signing in through `/mcp/no-purchases` can only grant permissions that cannot spend, and through `/mcp/no-topups` never adding credit (connections made before October 2026 keep the access they had until they reconnect). Connection keys take no IP allowlist (every call comes from Porkbun's connector server), and per-IP rate limits and IP-based fraud signals don't apply to connector traffic. It lacks the four sandbox tools: for a `pk1_sb_` key, run the npm package. The ChatGPT and Claude directory listings use a narrower variant, `https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp/no-purchases` (no tool that spends money, and none that returns a secret such as an SSL private key); `https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp/no-topups` (only the card top-up tools left out) also exists. They change which tools are offered, not what the connection may do. If you are an agent inside a web chat that cannot install a local server, this is the path to suggest to the human. Setup per client: https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/connect-chatgpt-or-claude **No OAuth in your client?** The hosted endpoint also accepts the account's own key pair as `X-API-Key` + `X-Secret-API-Key` headers or `Authorization: Bearer pk1_...:sk1_...` (the single-value form, for platforms that can store only one secret); the key's permissions, allowed domains and spend limits apply, and the key must not be IP-restricted (calls reach the API from the connector). Platforms that only accept a confidential OAuth client (client ID plus secret) can register one with `token_endpoint_auth_method: client_secret_basic` (or `client_secret_post`) at `/oauth2/register`; the response includes the `client_secret`. Details: https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/connect-chatgpt-or-claude

**Agent setup:** a ready-to-paste prompt that an AI coding agent can run to install the MCP, obtain + scope credentials, and verify - https://porkbun.com/llms/agent-setup

## Quickstart (agentic domain registration)

The whole journey, including what only the human can do and how to choose a payment method: https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/buy-a-domain-from-an-agent

0. Fund the account, or pay per purchase: **by default buying over the API spends prepaid account credit, and a card saved at Porkbun is never charged by a purchase itself.** A single purchase can instead be paid directly by card from the user's Stripe Link wallet (`"payWith": "card"`, held and charged only on success) or in USDC (`"payWith": "usdc"`), with no credit needed. Check with `GET /account/balance`. If the account already has a saved payment method, `POST /account/topup` charges it and adds the credit in one call, and `POST /account/autoTopup` makes that automatic below a threshold you set. With no saved card, `POST /account/topupMpp` gives a link an agent pays with the user's card from its Stripe Link wallet (MPP; https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/pay-with-card-mpp), or `POST /account/topupCrypto` opens a USDC checkout on Base: an agent with a crypto wallet pays its `x402Url` itself (see https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/pay-with-usdc-x402), or a person pays its `payUrl`. Otherwise add credit at https://porkbun.com/account/credit - a card can only be saved on the website. **Or skip funding entirely:** an agent with an x402 wallet can send `"payWith": "usdc"` on the purchase itself and pay the HTTP 402 it returns, so no credit is needed (https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/pay-with-usdc-x402). Also verify the account's email and phone, which registration requires: both can be verified from the agent, `POST /account/verifyEmail/send` and `/account/verifyPhone/send` sending a code to the address or phone on the account, then `/confirm` with the code the person reads out (https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/verify-the-account). Purchases and top-ups stay within the account's monthly limit, $100 a month until the account holder sets their own (https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/spend-limits).
1. Check availability + price: `POST https://api.porkbun.com/api/json/v3/domain/checkDomain/{domain}`
2. Rehearse: the same `/domain/create` call with `dryRun: true` (and `cost: 0` if you want to be quoted) returns `wouldSucceed`, `cost`, `balance` and, if you are short, `shortfall` - charging nothing
3. Register: `POST /domain/create/{domain}` with `cost` (price in pennies as integer, must match the quote), `agreeToTerms: "yes"`, and an `Idempotency-Key` header
4. Add DNS: `POST /dns/create/{domain}` with `type`, `content`, optional `ttl`

## Authentication

Pass `apikey` and `secretapikey` in the JSON body, or use `X-API-Key` / `X-Secret-API-Key` request headers (preferred for GET and agent frameworks). A short-lived bearer token is also available via `/auth/getToken` (`Authorization: Bearer <token>`). Create keys at https://porkbun.com/account/api

**Connected apps (OAuth).** Tokens issued by the Porkbun authorization server (`https://porkbun.com/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`) for the hosted MCP connector look like `pbo_at_...` and are sent as `Authorization: Bearer`. They are for MCP clients connecting to `https://mcp.porkbun.com/mcp`, not a general way to call the API; for your own code, use API keys.

**Partner-only endpoints exist and are not listed below:** `/auth/login` (authenticate a Porkbun user on a partner's behalf) and the `/abuse/*` family (registrant lookups, account enable/disable, EPP status changes, sinkholing) both need special access granted on the key, and return the same errors as an unknown endpoint without it. They are documented in the OpenAPI spec; ask support if you think you need them.

**Agent / app key handoff (PKCE).** An app that doesn't yet have keys can get them without ever handling the user's password: `POST /apikey/request` with a `codeChallenge` (S256) returns an `authUrl`; send the user there to approve (they can create a Porkbun account first if they don't have one), then call `/apikey/retrieve` with the matching `codeVerifier` to receive both keys once - the secret is never shown in the browser. Native/mobile apps can add a `returnUrl` (an HTTPS Universal Link / App Link) to be redirected back into the app after approval; only `status` + `requestToken` ride the redirect, never the key. Step-by-step for a mobile app (both existing and brand-new users): https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/onboard-a-mobile-app-user To get a key with only some permissions, add `"scopes": ["dns"]` (any of `read`, `dns`, `domains`, `email`, `hosting`, `purchase`, `funding`, `account`) to `/apikey/request`: the approval page shows them, the account holder can grant those or less (never more), and `/ping` on the new key reports what was granted. Over MCP: `request_api_key` (returns the approval link and the PKCE verifier) then `retrieve_api_key`.

**Revoking a key.** `POST /apikey/revoke` with `"confirm": "revoke"` permanently revokes the key making the call, and only that key (no key can touch another). Use it when an agent is done with a key or thinks it leaked; any key can call it, even a read-only one. It stops working within a few seconds; a key belonging to an OAuth-connected app disconnects that app. Other keys are listed, edited and revoked at https://porkbun.com/account/api.

**Sharing a website with someone (site sharing).** To let another person and their AI agent run ONE domain's website without the account: `POST /apikey/share` with `domain` and `sharedWith` (who it is for; optional `claimHours`, 1-168, default 24, the window to claim it; optional `accessHours`, 1-8760, how long the access lasts once claimed - leave out for until revoked, and when it runs out calls get `SHARE_ACCESS_ENDED`). Nothing is granted by that call: it returns an `approveUrl` the account holder must open and approve on porkbun.com - give it to them. Approving shows a one-time share link, a QR code, a share code and a `handoffPrompt` for the other person's agent; `GET /apikey/shares` returns the same once approved (link and prompt only to keys with full access or `account`). The other side claims once: their agent calls `POST /apikey/claim` with `{"shareToken": "..."}` (no API key needed; returns `apikey`/`secretapikey`, secret shown once), or in the Claude app or ChatGPT they add the Porkbun connector and enter the share code instead of logging in. The new key has the `site` permission alone, limited to that domain: it runs the website (WordPress content via `/hosting/wpRequest` and `/hosting/wpUploadMedia`, files, Link in Bio edits, backups/restores, staging, PHP/WP versions, SSL, search visibility) but cannot buy, cancel or change auto-renew, change DNS, turn on Link in Bio, or see anything account-wide (`INSUFFICIENT_SCOPE` / `DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED`). The owner is emailed on claim; `POST /apikey/revokeShare` (`id`) or deleting the "Share: <name>" key ends it, and the other side can give it back with `POST /apikey/revoke` (the owner is emailed). `SHARE_NOT_FOUND` = used, revoked, expired or wrong: ask for a new one. Guide: https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/share-site-access

## Key endpoints

- `GET/POST /ping` - verify credentials, get caller IP, and `account`: the username of the account the key belongs to. Errors that mean "not in this account" (`DOMAIN_NOT_FOUND`, `API_ACCESS_DISABLED`, the `/dns/*` `INVALID_DOMAIN`) name it too, so check it before concluding a domain is missing
- `GET/POST /ip` - caller IP, no auth
- `GET/POST /pricing/get` - registration, renewal and transfer prices (no auth). Filter with `tld` (one) and/or `tlds` (array, or comma-separated on GET): `GET /pricing/get?tld=io` or `?tlds=com,io,dev`. Case, a leading dot and IDN form (Unicode or punycode) are handled. TLDs Porkbun doesn't sell are listed in `unsupported` rather than priced; if none are sold -> `INVALID_TLD` (400). No filter returns every TLD (~900), so filter when you only need a few. Each TLD's `coupons` holds the public codes that work at checkout right now, keyed `registration` / `transfer` (empty when none applies)
- `POST /domain/checkDomain/{domain}` - availability + price (registration, renewal, transfer). For a name already in your account it adds `inYourAccount: true`: `price` is still the registration price, the renewal price is `additional.renewal.price`. For a name registered to someone else it adds `aftermarketSearch`: the name may be for sale (see `/aftermarket/search`). Rate limited to 10 checks per 10 seconds per account by default (a 10-second window, so a batch of candidate names can go back-to-back); `limits` in the response reports what is left. An account that checks ~1,800 names over three hours while buying fewer than one domain per 200 names checked is treated as scanning for 24 hours and gets 50 names per 5 minutes (`RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`, `reason: "SUSTAINED_BULK_CHECKING"`); ordinary checking never gets near it, and accounts with 100+ registrations a year and active affiliates are exempt
- `POST /domain/checkDomain` with `{"domains": [...]}` - **check up to 25 at once, and prefer this over looping the single form.** Separate budget of 200 domains per 60 seconds (counted per domain, not per call), because checks are chunked per registry and a batch costs us less than the same names one at a time. Returns `domains` keyed by name, plus `invalid` (not checkable - one typo does not fail the call) and `unresolved` (the registry did not answer; this is NOT "unavailable", retry them). Over 25 returns `BULK_CHECK_TOO_MANY` and checks nothing. Synchronous, no polling: ~3s for 25 mixed TLDs, but a batch heavy in low-cap TLDs (.de is one per command) is refused with `BULK_CHECK_TOO_SLOW` rather than risking a truncated response.
- `GET /domain/getRegistrationRequirements/{tld}` - is the TLD API-registerable + the create-request body as JSON Schema + any registry eligibility fields (e.g. .us nexus, .ca legal type). Call before create to validate eligibility/payload
- `POST /domain/create/{domain}` - register. Paid from prepaid account credit by default (a saved card is never charged by the purchase itself), or directly with `payWith` (below); a single API registration is capped at $100 (`ORDER_TOO_LARGE`) and premium names are website-only. **An account's first registration** can be made over the API, like any other. **Every registration includes a free email hosting trial mailbox** (`GET /email/getMailboxes/{domain}` shows it waiting; `POST /email/setupMailbox/{domain}` gives it an address for free, so don't buy one). **Internationalized names (IDNs)** under a TLD whose registry needs a language need `idnLanguage`, a code from the `idnLanguages` that `/domain/checkDomain` returns for them (no `idnLanguages` means none is needed); without it the call is refused before any charge with `IDN_LANGUAGE_REQUIRED`. Names may be sent in Unicode (`caf\u00e9.com`, that is cafe with an acute e) or punycode **Or pay in USDC directly:** add `"payWith": "usdc"` (also on renew, transfer, `/closeout/buy` and paid `/hosting/create`); the call answers HTTP 402 `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` with x402 terms in the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` header, an x402 client pays and repeats the same request with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`, and the purchase completes in that call. If the purchase fails after payment, the payment stays on the account as credit, not returned to the wallet.
- `POST /domain/renew/{domain}` - renew
- `GET /domain/getContacts/{domain}` , `POST /domain/updateContacts/{domain}` - read/edit the domain contacts (registrant, admin, tech, billing). Send any subset of roles; unspecified roles keep their current values. `state` is matched against the country's official list ignoring case, accents and short codes (`NJ`, `new jersey`, `NEW JERSEY` all become `New Jersey`), because some registries validate that field case-sensitively - .mx wants `Ciudad de M\u00e9xico` (Mexico with an acute e) for Mexico City and Porkbun substitutes it. On the .mx family a state matching nothing returns `INVALID_STATE` with every accepted value in `validStates`; elsewhere it is passed through unchanged. If the registry refuses a new contact, nothing is changed and the error says what it objected to
- `POST /domain/transfer/{domain}` - initiate inbound transfer (needs `authCode`)
- `GET /domain/getTransfer/{domain}` , `GET /domain/listTransfers` - transfer status
- `POST /domain/transfer/{domain}` with `holdForDnsSetup: true` - **the no-downtime path**. Charges the transfer but parks it at `PENDINGDNS` instead of releasing it, so the zone can be built before the domain moves. Nothing releases a held transfer on a timer. Not available for .uk/Handshake (`TRANSFER_HOLD_NOT_AVAILABLE`, not charged)
- `GET /domain/getTransferSetup/{domain}` - where a held transfer is and what it waits on (held? zone ready? record count? current delegation? next step)
- `POST /domain/prepareTransfer/{domain}` - create the DNS zone for a held transfer; returns the Porkbun nameservers
- `POST /domain/startTransfer/{domain}` - release a held transfer. Refuses on an empty zone (`TRANSFER_ZONE_EMPTY`) unless `force: true`
- `POST /domain/cancelTransfer/{domain}` - cancel and refund. Marks locally, withdraws at the registry, **verifies** the withdrawal, then refunds; if the registry state can't be confirmed it restores the row and returns `TRANSFER_STATE_UNCONFIRMED` rather than refunding a possibly-live transfer
- `POST /domain/updateTransferAuthCode/{domain}` - replace the auth code on a transfer that stalled on a bad one and re-queue it, instead of cancel/refund/resubmit. The new code is registry-validated before it is stored
- `GET /domain/get/{domain}` - single domain detail
- `GET/POST /domain/listAll` - list/filter domains (`?tlds[]=`, `?expiringWithinDays=`, `?autoRenew=`, `?apiAccess=`, `?nameContains=`, `?sortName=`, `?start=`). Date filters, `YYYY-MM-DD` or date-time, UTC: `addedAfter`/`addedBefore` (when the domain joined the account, by registration or transfer: `addedDate`; pass the newest `addedDate` seen to sync only new domains), `createdAfter`/`createdBefore` (registry creation date, which a transfer keeps, so not "new in my account"), `expiresAfter`/`expiresBefore`. `sortName=added_date` sorts by `addedDate`
- `POST /domain/updateAutoRenew/{domain}` - turn auto-renew on/off. Takes `status: "on"|"off"`, and a `domains` array for several at once; each domain is reported separately in `results`, so a partial failure does not fail the call
- `GET /domain/getUrlForwarding/{domain}` , `POST /domain/addUrlForward/{domain}` , `POST /domain/deleteUrlForward/{domain}/{id}` - URL forwarding. Forwarding is served by our nameservers, so like any DNS change it does nothing while the domain is delegated elsewhere
- `GET /domain/getGlue/{domain}` , `POST /domain/createGlue/{domain}/{subdomain}` , `POST /domain/updateGlue/{domain}/{subdomain}` , `POST /domain/deleteGlue/{domain}/{subdomain}` - glue records (host objects), needed when the domain's own nameservers live under it (ns1.example.com for example.com). `updateGlue` REPLACES the address set rather than adding to it. `getGlue` returns `glue`: `[{host, v4, v6}]` (both arrays always present; `hosts` is the same data as `[hostname, {v4, v6}]` pairs, kept for older clients)
- `GET/POST /dns/retrieve/{domain}` - get DNS records
- `GET/POST /dns/retrieveByNameType/{domain}/{type}/{subdomain}` - the same records filtered to one name and type; omit the subdomain for the apex. Cheaper than pulling the zone and filtering client-side
- `GET /dns/scan/{domain}` - discover what the domain currently publishes by querying its **live** nameservers; writes nothing. Run this BEFORE a transfer moves the nameservers, because a transfer carries no zone data and the old registrar's records become unreadable the moment it stops answering. Thorough but not exhaustive (DNS cannot list a zone; AXFR is refused). 20 calls/hour
- `POST /dns/import/{domain}` - bulk-create records, either an exact `records` list you supply or whatever a scan finds. Idempotent: already-present records come back as `skipped`, not failures. Max 500/call. Records do nothing until the domain points at Porkbun's nameservers
- `POST /dns/create/{domain}` , `POST /dns/edit/{domain}/{id}` , `POST /dns/delete/{domain}/{id}` - manage DNS. Creating a record that already exists with the same name/type/content returns HTTP 400 `DUPLICATE_RECORD` with the existing record's id in `existingId` (adopt it, don't retry); a write blocked by CNAME exclusivity returns `RECORD_CONFLICT` with the blocking rows in `conflictingRecords`. A zone is capped at 2,500 records; past that, creates return `ZONE_RECORD_LIMIT`. Editing a record to the values it already holds succeeds as a no-op, so you can write desired state unconditionally. **Read `warnings` on every write.** We hold a zone for every domain in the account whether or not the domain is delegated to us, so a write to a domain pointing at someone else's nameservers still returns `SUCCESS` - stored here, invisible to the world. When that is the case the response carries a `warnings` string naming the nameservers that actually answer and how to fix it. `status` stays `SUCCESS` and the write did happen; `warnings` is absent when there is nothing to say
- `GET /dns/preflight/{domain}?intent=move-nameservers` - **ask before you break something.** Read-only; changes nothing. Returns `blockers` (will break), `warnings` (will not break outright but the customer will notice) and every `check` that ran, each naming its rule with a `next_action`. `intent` is one of general, move-nameservers, transfer-out, enable-dnssec. The blockers worth knowing: `dnssec-active` (DS records published means new nameservers serve answers that do not match them and validating resolvers refuse the whole zone - the domain goes DARK, so remove DNSSEC and wait for the DS TTL first), `spf-duplicate` and `spf-lookups` (both RFC 7208 permerrors that fail SPF for every sender), `mx-undeliverable`, `cname-exclusivity` (RFC 1034). `nameservers-ours` is the one to check first: it says whether this zone is what the world resolves at all, including the mixed case where only some of the delegated nameservers are ours and resolvers disagree query to query. The one people have never heard of is `wildcard-shadowed`: under RFC 4592 a wildcard answers only names that do NOT exist, so a name holding just an MX or TXT record stops inheriting the wildcard address and goes dark with nothing in the zone looking wrong.
- `GET /dns/history/{domain}` - **DNS has an undo.** Every version of the zone we hold, newest first, each with `takenAt`, why it was taken, the record count AS IT WAS then, and `matchesLive`. Points are captured automatically before the first write to a zone each hour, before any bulk import or wipe, and before any restore - so you do not need the customer to remember what the record said.
- `GET /dns/diff/{domain}/{snapshotId}` - `missing` (in the point, not live - a restore adds these) and `extra` (live, not in the point - a restore leaves these unless you prune). Compared on name+type+content+priority, not id. SOA and NS excluded.
- `POST /dns/restore/{domain}` with `{"snapshotId": N}` - puts the zone back. Adds what is missing; `prune: true` also deletes what is extra. Supports `dryRun`. **The restore is itself reversible**: the pre-restore state is saved and returned as `previousStateSavedAs`. Read `failed` - parking/ALIAS/HTTPS records are managed elsewhere and are reported there rather than counted as restored.
- `GET /dns/getDnssecRecords/{domain}` , `POST /dns/createDnssecRecord/{domain}` , `POST /dns/deleteDnssecRecord/{domain}/{keytag}` - manage DNSSEC at the registry

*Semantics that trip agents up:* DNSSEC algorithms and digest types are validated **per registry**, not globally. Registries are retiring the values deprecated by RFC 9904/9905/9906 on their own schedules, so a value one registry has already dropped may still be accepted by another. A refused value returns `DNSSEC_ALGORITHM_DEPRECATED` before anything is sent to the registry; a value that still works but is being retired returns `SUCCESS` with a `warnings` array, which is advisory: the record WAS created. Algorithm 8 (RSA/SHA-256) or 13 (ECDSA/SHA-256) with digest type 2 (SHA-256) is accepted everywhere. Deprecation never affects reads or deletes: an existing record keeps resolving and can always be removed, whatever it is signed with.

- `GET/POST /ssl/retrieve/{domain}` - SSL bundle
- `GET /account/balance` - account credit balance
- `POST /account/invite` , `GET /account/inviteStatus` - create a one-time signup invite (token + URL) for a prospective customer and poll whether they completed it. The user finishes registration in the browser, so CAPTCHA, address and ToS are handled there; the invite expires in 48 hours and is single-use
- `GET|POST /account/autoTopup` - read or set top-up settings. `amount` (what a top-up adds) stands alone: `{"amount": 10000}` sets it without automating anything, because `POST /account/topup` charges the same figure. Add `enabled: true` + `threshold` to also fire it automatically when the balance falls below that; `enabled: false` stops the automation and keeps the amount. Amounts set over the API are capped at $500 ($5 floor); one the account holder sets on the website is honoured as-is. `paymentMethodOnFile: false` means the settings are inert - a card can only be saved on the website. `cards` lists the saved cards (up to 3), primary first then backups, each with `status` (`active`/`expired`/`declined`), `lastDeclineCode` and `retryAfter`; a Link wallet shows `usedForTopups: false` because top-ups charge cards only. Cards are added, removed and reordered on the website only
- `POST /account/topup` - **charge the saved payment method now** and add the credit, for when you are already stuck on `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS`. `amount` (integer US cents, 500-50000) is optional: omit it and you get the account's configured top-up amount, or $50 if none was ever set (`amountSource` says which of configured/default/request applied). Passing one charges that figure for this call only and does NOT rewrite the stored setting - use it rather than calling /account/autoTopup to set an amount you only need once. An amount set via the API is capped at $500. Monthly dollars are capped too: the account's monthly spend limit bounds top-ups as well as domain spend, and an account with no limit set gets a $100/month top-up ceiling (`monthlyCeiling` / `ceilingSource` on `GET /account/autoTopup`). Also 5 top-ups per day and 20 per month (`TOPUP_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`), It charges the **primary card and falls back to the backups** if it is declined (at most one card charged; no fallback after a fraud-type decline): the response's `card` is the one that paid, `usedBackup: true` means the primary was declined (it is in `declinedFirst`) - tell the account holder their primary card needs attention. `NO_PAYMENT_METHOD` when there is nothing to charge, `CARD_DECLINED` when every card tried refused (`declined` lists each card and decline code). Sandbox keys get simulated credit. Supports `dryRun`
- `GET /account/apiSettings` - spend-control settings, this month's spend, and the limits actually enforced (`spendLimit`, `topupLimit`)
- `POST /account/verifyPhone/send`, `POST /account/verifyPhone/confirm` - verify the phone number on the account without leaving the agent: `send` texts (or, with `"channel": "call"`, calls) a code to it, ask the person for the code, then `confirm` with `{"code": "..."}`. Clears the phone half of `VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`; the response says whether the email is verified too. Some countries must verify on the website (`PHONE_VERIFY_UNAVAILABLE`)
- `POST /account/verifyEmail/send`, `POST /account/verifyEmail/confirm` - the same for the email address on the account: `send` emails the verification message (link plus code), the person (or whoever reads that inbox) gives you the code, then `confirm` with `{"code": "..."}`. The code is never returned by the API or a webhook. Errors `EMAIL_CODE_INVALID`, `EMAIL_VERIFY_LIMIT`, `EMAIL_VERIFY_UNAVAILABLE`. Webhooks `account.verification.code_sent` and `account.verification.completed` announce a sent code and a finished verification
- `POST /account/topupCrypto` - open a Coinbase checkout to add credit with **USDC on Base** (`amount` in cents, $1-$500). Returns `x402Url`, which an agent with a wallet pays itself over x402 (gasless, no page), and `payUrl` for a person. Nothing is charged by the call; credit lands when the payment confirms, less Coinbase's ~1% fee (`estimatedCredit_cents`). To cover an `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` shortfall exactly, use its `usdcAmountToCover`. The way past `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` when no card is saved. Needs verified email and phone (`CRYPTO_NOT_AVAILABLE` for bank-transfer-only accounts); not on sandbox keys
- `POST /account/topupMpp` - a signed, single-use link an agent pays with the **user's card** over MPP (Machine Payments Protocol) using a Stripe Shared Payment Token from its Link Agent Wallet: POST the link, get 402 with a `Payment` challenge, retry with the credential, credit lands immediately. No card needs to be saved at Porkbun. Same limits as `/account/topup`. Guide: https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/pay-with-card-mpp
- `GET /account/topupCryptoStatus/{checkoutId}` - `state` ACTIVE / PROCESSING / COMPLETED (credited) / EXPIRED / FAILED, plus the balance
- `GET /account/invoices` - the account's invoices (one per order), newest first. Optional `year`, `start`, `limit` (max 100). `total_cents` is net of refunds and `state` is `PAID`, `PARTIALLY_REFUNDED`, `REFUNDED` or `UNPAID`; each carries `url`, its page on porkbun.com
- `GET /account/invoice/{orderId}` - one invoice as data: `billTo`, `paymentMethods` (card brand + last four), `items` (term, resulting domain `expires`, status, `price_cents`, `discount_cents`), `gross_cents`/`refunded_cents`/`total_cents`. Same figures as the PDF. `downloadUrl` downloads the PDF without signing in for 15 minutes: hand the user that rather than rebuilding the file from base64. `INVOICE_NOT_FOUND` for an ID not on this account
- `GET /account/invoicePdf/{orderId}` - the invoice PDF, base64 in `contentBase64` with `filename`; the same document as Download PDF on porkbun.com. `INVOICE_PDF_FAILED` means retry (the JSON form still works)
- `POST /marketplace/getAll` - Porkbun Marketplace listings (names customers list themselves) with filters. For all aftermarkets at once use `/aftermarket/search`
- `GET /aftermarket/search` - registered domains that are for sale: Afternic, Sedo, Atom, NameBright and DAX listings and auctions, plus Porkbun Marketplace, merged to the lowest price per name. `query` is a keyword or a full domain (its listing comes back as `exactMatch`); filters `tld`, `saleType` (`buy_now`/`make_offer`/`auction`), `priceMin`/`priceMax` (cents), `limit`. **Read `saleType`: only `buy_now` prices are prices; `make_offer` is the seller's minimum offer and `auction` the current bid.** Read-only: the user buys on porkbun.com through each listing's `buyUrl`, and the name arrives by transfer within days. 20 searches a minute per account
- `GET /closeout/search` - search expired-domain closeouts. Filters: `query`, `tld`, `nameLength`, `ageMin`/`ageMax`, `priceMin`/`priceMax` (cents), `start`/`limit`; sort by `domain|endTime|price|revenue|visitors|inboundLinks|registrationDate` x `asc|desc` (`registrationDate` + `asc` = OLDEST first, which is how you find aged names; `asc` on revenue/visitors/inboundLinks lists no-data rows first, so use `desc` there). Returns `age` and `registrationDate` on every row, plus `totalAvailable` for paging. `price` is the closeout price ALONE
- `GET /closeout/get/{domain}` - one closeout plus `totalPrice`, the binding amount (`price` + the renewal-or-transfer year). Cannot be derived from search: a name already at Porkbun is renewed, anything else is transferred in, and those price differently
- `POST /closeout/buy/{domain}` - buy one. `cost` must equal `totalPrice` exactly (`COST_MISMATCH` otherwise); `dryRun` + `cost:0` quotes. Charges account credit and claims the name; the domain is **reserved, not delivered** - the provider releases it over the following days, so poll `/domain/listAll` or use the `domain.registered` webhook. Post-charge failures refund automatically with `refunded: true`, including losing the race (`CLOSEOUT_UNAVAILABLE`, not worth retrying on the same name)
- `GET /webhook/eventTypes` - subscribable event-type catalog
- `GET /webhook/list` , `GET /webhook/get/{id}` - list / fetch webhook endpoints (each endpoint's signing `secret` is included only for keys with full access or the `account` scope; read-only keys get it omitted)
- `POST /webhook/create` - register an HTTPS endpoint (returns the signing secret). The URL must be `https://` on port 443 with a hostname resolving to a **public** internet address, and must not embed credentials; private/loopback/link-local/CGNAT/reserved targets are refused with `INVALID_WEBHOOK_URL`. A not-yet-resolving hostname is accepted so you can register before deploying the receiver, but the rules are re-checked (and the connection pinned to the vetted address) immediately before every delivery
- `POST /webhook/update` - change url/events/status (ACTIVE|DISABLED)
- `POST /webhook/rotateSecret` , `POST /webhook/test` , `POST /webhook/delete` - rotate secret, send a test event, delete
- `GET /webhook/deliveries` , `GET /webhook/delivery/{id}` - recent delivery log (~30 days) + single delivery with full payload
- `POST /webhook/resend` - re-queue a past delivery (reuses the original event id)
### Cloudflare connect - move domains to the customer's own Cloudflare account

We create the zone in their Cloudflare account, copy across the DNS records we hold, and repoint the registry nameservers. Two stages, and the first needs a human.

**Stage 1 - connect the Cloudflare account (browser, one time).** Cloudflare's consent screen can't be completed over the API, and the authorization is bound to the Porkbun web session that starts it. So: send the account owner to `https://porkbun.com/account/connectCloudflare`, then poll.
- `GET /cloudflare/getConnection` - `connected` true/false, which Cloudflare account it points at, and a `connectUrl` + `nextStep` when a human still has to act. **This is the poll target.**
- `POST /cloudflare/disconnect` - forget the grant (domains already moved stay on Cloudflare)

**Stage 2 - move domains (fully API).**
- `GET /cloudflare/inventory` - every domain with `state` (`eligible`/`warn`/`blocked`/`connected`/`inprogress`) and a human `reason`. Read this first; works before the account is connected, so an agent can plan while the owner authorizes
- `POST /cloudflare/connect` - queue one or many (`{"domains":["a.com","b.com"]}`, `dryRun`-able). **Asynchronous**: returns *queued*, never *connected*
- `GET /cloudflare/getQueue` - every move ever requested (rows are never deleted, so it's the audit trail too)
- `GET /cloudflare/get/{domain}` - one domain's progress, zone id, and the nameservers we replaced
- `POST /cloudflare/retry/{domain}` - re-queue a failure
- `GET /cloudflare/preview/{domain}` - exactly which records a move would copy/drop, without queueing
- `GET /cloudflare/getRecords/{domain}` - the domain's **live** records at Cloudflare with their proxied state. After a move this is authoritative; `/dns/retrieve` reads the Porkbun zone, which no longer answers
- `GET /cloudflare/getZone/{domain}` - Cloudflare's own zone state (status, its nameservers) plus `nameserversDrifted` if someone repointed NS elsewhere
- `POST /cloudflare/setProxy/{domain}` - turn the Cloudflare proxy on/off (`{"enabled":true}`, optional `records:["@","www"]`). **The move always imports DNS-only (grey) on purpose**; proxying is a separate explicit step, best done after confirming the site still serves. Only A/AAAA/CNAME are proxiable; warns if MX points at a name you're proxying
- `POST /cloudflare/createRecord/{domain}` , `POST /cloudflare/editRecord/{domain}/{recordId}` , `POST /cloudflare/deleteRecord/{domain}/{recordId}` - **write DNS in the zone that actually answers.** After a move these are the endpoints that change resolution; `/dns/*` does not. `name` takes `@` or a bare label, MX needs `priority`, `proxied` is A/AAAA/CNAME only, structured types (SRV/CAA) take a `data` object. All `dryRun`-able
- `GET /cloudflare/getZoneSettings/{domain}` / `POST /cloudflare/setZoneSettings/{domain}` - allowlisted zone settings (`ssl`, `always_use_https`, `automatic_https_rewrites`, `min_tls_version`, `development_mode`, `cache_level`). Warns when `ssl` is `flexible`/`off` (Cloudflare fetches the origin over plain HTTP while visitors see a padlock). Returns `CLOUDFLARE_REAUTHORIZE_REQUIRED` + `connectUrl` if the grant predates the `zone-settings.write` scope
- `POST /cloudflare/rollback/{domain}` - undo: nameservers back to Porkbun (the Cloudflare zone is left alone; deleting it is the customer's call)

*The no-downtime transfer sequence:* submit with `holdForDnsSetup: true` -> `POST /domain/prepareTransfer/{domain}` -> `POST /dns/import/{domain}` -> `POST /domain/startTransfer/{domain}`. Held transfers wait indefinitely for that last call, and it refuses to release into an empty zone. Note `/dns/*` will not accept a domain that is neither in the account nor covered by a pending transfer with a prepared zone - that is why the hold comes first.

*A transfer does not carry DNS.* Registrar transfers move the delegation only - EPP has no concept of zone contents - so a domain whose records were never recreated at Porkbun goes dark the moment the losing registrar drops the zone. Capture with `GET /dns/scan/{domain}` **while the old nameservers still answer**, recreate with `POST /dns/import/{domain}`, and only then move the nameservers. Porkbun also snapshots a pending inbound transfer's zone on its own and restores it after the transfer completes if the Porkbun zone is still empty, but do not rely on that as the primary path - an explicit capture is exact, and a scan cannot enumerate a zone.

*Nameservers are an unordered set.* `/domain/getNs` reads live from the registry, and registries return the set in whatever order they like - it will often differ from the order you sent to `/domain/updateNs`. Order is meaningless in DNS (NS is an RRset, RFC 1034/2181) and is not preserved by the parent zone, so compare nameservers as a set. Modelling them as an ordered list produces permanent false drift.

*Two DNS surfaces:* `/dns/*` manages **Porkbun's** nameservers; `/cloudflare/*Record` manages the customer's **Cloudflare** zone after a move. *Once a domain is connected, Porkbun DNS is no longer authoritative for it.* `/dns/*` writes still succeed against the Porkbun zone (kept in step in case you roll back) but do NOT change what resolves - those responses carry a `warnings` entry saying so. Read `/cloudflare/getRecords/{domain}` for what Cloudflare actually serves. Subscribe to `cloudflare.connect.completed` / `cloudflare.connect.failed` webhooks instead of polling.

*Queue status values:* `queued` -> `working` -> `setup` -> `activating` -> `connected`/`done`; terminal states are `connected`/`done`, `skipped`, `failed`/`error` and `undone`. **Neither `setup` nor `activating` is terminal** - in `setup` the zone exists in the customer's Cloudflare account but Cloudflare has not provisioned it yet and the nameservers have NOT been touched (the domain still resolves from Porkbun); in `activating` the nameservers are already repointed and Cloudflare is confirming the zone, which is legitimately slow (registry + resolver propagation, allow up to 72h - 59h has been observed on a move that then succeeded). Keep polling. If the domain **stops resolving** while Cloudflare has not activated it, that is not waited out: its nameservers go back to Porkbun within minutes and the row is reported `undone`. A `failed` row that was waiting on Cloudflare is re-checked for up to 30 days, so a late activation still ends up reported as connected rather than staying failed. **A big batch paces itself:** zone creation stops while the customer's Cloudflare account has several domains still awaiting activation (Cloudflare refuses to add more, and cannot be hurried), so rows can sit in `queued` with a message explaining the wait - that is not a stall to retry around.

*Semantics that trip agents up:* `skipped` is a NORMAL outcome, not an error - DNSSEC live, custom nameservers, already connected each come back per-domain with a reason, so read the reasons instead of treating a non-empty `skipped` as failure. Eligibility is re-checked immediately before each domain is acted on, so a domain accepted at queue time can still be skipped later. Re-submitting a domain is safe and idempotent. Limits: 500 domains per call, 2000 per account per hour. Not available with sandbox keys (a real Cloudflare grant can't be simulated).

### Email - forwarding and mailboxes
- `GET /email/getForwards/{domain}`, `POST /email/addForward/{domain}` (`{"address": "info", "forwardTo": "me@example.net"}`), `POST /email/deleteForward/{domain}` (same body) - email forwarding: deliver an address at the domain to another mailbox. Free up to the domain's limit (20 by default, `limits`); an address may forward to several mailboxes, so delete names both. No catch-all/wildcard (`WILDCARD_NOT_SUPPORTED`). Adding sets up Porkbun's MX and SPF at the apex; **if that would delete another mail service's MX records or rewrite an existing SPF record, the call returns `DNS_CHANGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED` with `dnsChanges` - tell the user what changes and resend with `"confirmDnsChanges": true` only with their OK.** `dryRun` previews. Deleting the last forward removes those DNS records. If the domain uses other nameservers, forwarding needs Porkbun's MX records there too. Guide: https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/set-up-email-forwarding
- `GET /email/getMailboxes/{domain}`, `POST /email/setupMailbox/{domain}` (`{"address": "me"}`), `POST /email/createMailbox/{domain}` (`{"address": "me", "cost": 3600, "agreeToTerms": "yes"}`) - email hosting mailboxes (IMAP/POP/SMTP + webmail). Every domain registration includes a free trial mailbox waiting to be set up (`status: PENDINGSETUP`); `setupMailbox` gives a waiting mailbox its address for free, `createMailbox` buys one ($36.00 a year, renews automatically; tell the user the price first) and sets it up, paid from credit or with `payWith` card/usdc. Leave out `password` and a strong one is generated and **returned once** - give it to the user right away. Same DNS confirmation as forwarding (`DNS_CHANGE_CONFIRMATION_REQUIRED`). Needs a verified email and phone. DKIM/DMARC are set up on the website. Set-up mailboxes renew on their own when due (`autoRenews`, `renewalPrice` in `getMailboxes`); `POST /email/renewMailbox/{domain}` (`{"address": "me", "cost": 3600, "agreeToTerms": "yes"}`) adds a year now, e.g. to keep a trial mailbox. While the domain is expired neither happens: renew the domain first (`renewMailbox` returns `DOMAIN_EXPIRED`). Guide: https://porkbun.com/llms/guides/set-up-a-mailbox
- `POST /email/setPassword` - change a mailbox's password. Email endpoints are not simulated in the sandbox (`SANDBOX_UNSUPPORTED`)

### Hosting - static sites, WordPress sites and paid Link in Bio share these endpoints
Pick the product with the `sku` you pass to `/hosting/create`: **Secure Static Hosting** (`PIXIESECURESTATIC...`, you upload files), **Cloud for WordPress** (`CLOUDWORDPRESS...`, a managed WordPress site you drive through WordPress) or paid **Link in Bio** (`PIXIELINKSM1` / `PIXIELINKSY1`, a page of links edited with the `/linkinbio` endpoints; the free plan is `/linkinbio/create`). A domain's first purchase of a product is a 15-day free trial that auto-renews at the plan price; one free trial per domain per product.

*All three products:*
- `GET/POST /hosting/plans` - the plans you can buy (SKU, price, interval, trial length, features); `product` says which is which (`secureStaticHosting`, `cloudWordPress`, `managedLinks` = Link in Bio), and each row has `displayName`, `bestFor` (when to choose it) and `featuresText` (plain words; in `features`, bandwidth 0 = unmetered). Rule of thumb: a site you build and maintain as files = static; a site the owner edits, or that needs plugins = WordPress; just links = Link in Bio
- `POST /hosting/create/{domain}` - buy by `sku`, with the same row's `price` as `acknowledgedCost` and `agreeToTerms: "yes"`; gates the nameserver switch behind `agreeToNameserverChange`; `dryRun`-able. A WordPress sku's response includes `wordpress.restUrl` / `adminUrl`; a Link in Bio sku over a free page upgrades it and keeps the content
- `GET /hosting/get/{domain}` - status (product, plan, trial, expiry, auto-renew); after buying static hosting, poll until `ACTIVE` before deploying
- `POST /hosting/updateAutoRenew/{domain}` - `{"autoRenew": false}` turns auto-renew off (the plan runs to `expireDate`, is not charged again, then is removed; a paid Link in Bio falls back to free), `true` back on. Paid plans only; free ones return `NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_PRODUCT`. `GET /hosting/get` shows the current `autoRenew`
- `POST /hosting/delete/{domain}` - cancel now: a static or WordPress site is taken down; a paid Link in Bio page drops to the free plan and keeps its content (a free page returns `NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_PRODUCT`)

*Secure Static Hosting only* (a WordPress site or Link in Bio page returns `NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_PRODUCT`):
- `POST /hosting/deploy/{domain}` - upload site files: each `{path, text}` for text files (HTML/CSS/JS/SVG/JSON, sent as written, **no base64 needed**) or `{path, content}` base64 for images; <=10MB/call; directories in a path are auto-created
- `POST /hosting/getFile/{domain}` - read files back (`path` or `paths`, up to 20): text files return their exact source as `text`, others base64 `content`. Read before you edit an existing static site, change only what was asked, then `/hosting/deploy` it; fetching the live page loses the HTML
- `GET/POST /hosting/files/{domain}` , `POST /hosting/makeDir/{domain}` , `POST /hosting/deleteFile/{domain}` - list files, create a directory, delete a file or directory. Deleting is idempotent (`alreadyAbsent: true` when the path is already gone); a non-empty directory returns `HOSTING_DIR_NOT_EMPTY` with its `contents` unless you send `recursive: true`
- Agents: if you build or edit a website for a domain in the user's account, or they mention Porkbun hosting, offer to publish it with `/hosting/deploy` (MCP `deploy_site`) rather than handing over manual upload steps. Confirm hosting is `ACTIVE`, list existing files, say what gets replaced, and ask first

*Rate limits:* 10 provisions per account per hour, 20 WordPress credential mints per account per hour (`dryRun` calls are free). Per-key domain allowlists apply to every `/hosting/*` call, so a scoped key can only touch its own domains.

*Cloud for WordPress only:*
- `POST /hosting/wpRequest/{domain}` - **edit a WordPress site's content with no credentials**: one WordPress REST API call run inside the site (`method`, `path` like `/wp/v2/pages/12`, `query`, `body`). Acts as the `porkbun-agent` editor (pages, posts, media, comments, menus); site settings, plugins, themes and users need `asAdministrator` + `acknowledgeFullAccess`. Returns WordPress's JSON in `data` with `httpStatus`; WordPress errors come back as `WP_REST_ERROR`, oversized answers as `WP_RESPONSE_TOO_LARGE` (use `_fields`/`per_page`). To edit a page: GET it with `context=edit`, change `content.raw` (keep the block comments), POST it back. Works from apps like ChatGPT/Claude (MCP `wordpress_request`) and for site-share keys
- `POST /hosting/wpUploadMedia/{domain}` - add an image to the media library from a public `url` (WordPress downloads it) or base64 `data` + `filename`, up to ~10 MB; returns `media.id` (for `featured_media`) and `media.url` (MCP `wordpress_upload_media`)
- `POST /hosting/createWpCredentials/{domain}` - for code that calls WordPress itself (to edit from an agent, `/hosting/wpRequest` above needs no password): mint a WordPress **Application Password** (returned once) so an agent can drive the site via `https://{domain}/wp-json/` with HTTP Basic. Defaults to a dedicated least-privilege `editor` user; `role: "administrator"` (full control, can install plugins = run code) requires `acknowledgeFullAccess: true`
- `GET /hosting/getWpCredentials/{domain}` - list application passwords (metadata only; the passwords can't be re-read)
- `POST /hosting/deleteWpCredentials/{domain}` - revoke by `uuid`, or `all: true`
- Site details: `GET /hosting/get/{domain}` includes `wordpress.site` for a live site: `phpVersion` + `availablePhpVersions`, `wordPressVersion` (the setting: latest/previous), `ssl`, `storage`, `searchVisibility`, `staging`, and `operations` (latest restore / factory reset / site copy, with `state` queued/running/done/failed). Takes ~2s (it asks WP Cloud)
- `POST /hosting/setPhpVersion/{domain}` (`version`, one of `availablePhpVersions`), `POST /hosting/setWordPressVersion/{domain}` (`latest` or `previous` = one major release back, no pinned numbers), `POST /hosting/reissueSsl/{domain}` (stuck certificate; once per 5 min), `POST /hosting/setSearchVisibility/{domain}` (`visible` true/false)
- Backups: `GET/POST /hosting/backups/{domain}` (newest first, `limit` default 100, `type` files/database; automatic files daily + database hourly, kept 30 days), `POST /hosting/createBackup/{domain}` (one on-demand of each type; delete the old one first or it fails with "Quota Reached"), `POST /hosting/deleteBackup/{domain}` (`id`, on-demand only), `POST /hosting/restoreBackup/{domain}` (`fsId` + `dbId`; **replaces the site**, queued, site down a few minutes, poll `/hosting/get` `operations`; dry-run it and confirm with the user). Add `"staging": true` to any backup call for the staging copy
- Staging (a private copy on `*.stagebun.com`): `GET/POST /hosting/getStaging/{domain}` (url, status, job + state, password, outbound blocking, environment; `hosting` permission, it returns the password), `POST /hosting/createStaging/{domain}` (from live, or `fsId`+`dbId`; one per site; starts password protected with email blocked), `POST /hosting/resetStaging/{domain}` (rebuild, replaces staging), `POST /hosting/publishStaging/{domain}` (**replaces live** with staging after a safety backup of live; confirm first), `POST /hosting/deleteStaging/{domain}`. All queued: poll getStaging. Settings: `POST /hosting/setStagingGate/{domain}` (`enabled`, `password` 4-64), `POST /hosting/setStagingGuard/{domain}` (`blockEmail`, `blockApiRequests`), `POST /hosting/setStagingEnvironment/{domain}` (`staging`/`production`)
- `POST /sandbox/topup` , `POST /sandbox/reset` , `POST /sandbox/triggerWebhook` - sandbox only (pk1_sb_ keys): add fake credit / reset to a clean slate / fire a sample webhook event to your endpoints
- `GET /mock` , `GET|POST /mock/<path>` - credential-free mock server: schema-accurate example responses for any endpoint (append `?status=error` for the error shape)

### Link in Bio - a single page of links on a domain
A page is served on the domain itself, or (the free plan most .com domains registered at Porkbun already have) the domain forwards to `<domain-with-dashes>.l.ink`. Edits show up at once on the page and in the editor on porkbun.com. Reading needs the `read` permission, editing `hosting`; every write supports `dryRun`; not available with sandbox keys.
- `GET/POST /linkinbio/get/{domain}` - the page: `url`, `delivery` (domain / l.ink), `plan`, `features` (what the plan allows), `profile`, `links` (with `id`, in display order), `socials`, `appearance`, `settings`. Call it first: `LINKINBIO_NOT_FOUND` means there is no page yet
- `POST /linkinbio/create/{domain}` - turn on a free page on the domain (PIXIELINKS2M1: 50 links, no scheduling, animation, passcode protection or analytics IDs). Needs Porkbun nameservers (`agreeToNameserverChange: true` to switch). Starts with a placeholder title, bio and link: replace them
- Paid plan: `POST /hosting/create/{domain}` with `sku` `PIXIELINKSM1` ($3/month) or `PIXIELINKSY1` ($30/year), 1000 links and every feature. Over a free page it **upgrades in place and keeps the content**. `/hosting/delete` on a paid page moves it back to the free plan; nothing is deleted. A free page can't be turned off through the API (`NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_PRODUCT`); point the domain elsewhere to stop showing it
- `POST /linkinbio/updateProfile/{domain}` - `title`, `bio`, `avatar` (base64 JPEG/PNG, <=5MB; null removes)
- `POST /linkinbio/addLink/{domain}` - `title`, `url` (http/https only; a bare host gets https://), `type` (`link`, `featured`, or `category` = a heading with no url), `enabled`, `position` (`bottom` default, or `top`), and on paid plans `startDate`/`endDate` (UTC), `animation` (pulse/bounce/shake), `protection` (`{"type":"code","value":"1234"}`; `birthday` with value 18/21/25 and `sensitive` work on every plan)
- `POST /linkinbio/editLink/{domain}` (`id` + any of those fields; `enabled: false` hides a link), `POST /linkinbio/deleteLink/{domain}` (`id`), `POST /linkinbio/reorderLinks/{domain}` (`ids`: every link id in the new order)
- `POST /linkinbio/updateSocials/{domain}` - `location` (top/bottom), `socials` `{instagram, email, facebook, tiktok, youtube, twitter, linkedin}`: handle or URL, "" removes
- `POST /linkinbio/updateAppearance/{domain}` - `preset` (classic, ocean, midnight, paper, forest, sunset), `fontFamily`, `buttonStyle`, `radius` (0-50), `pageBackgroundMode` (solid/gradient), hex colours; null resets one
- `POST /linkinbio/updateSettings/{domain}` - `sensitiveContent` (generic, 18, 21, 25 or null) and, on paid plans, `analytics` IDs and UTM parameters
- A feature the plan lacks returns `FEATURE_NOT_IN_PLAN` and saves nothing; too many links `LINK_LIMIT_REACHED`; same title and URL as another link `DUPLICATE_LINK`

## Error codes (selection)
- `ACCOUNT_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED` - a new account was flagged for identity verification at signup (about 1 in 5); every call fails until the account holder completes it at `verificationUrl` (https://porkbun.com/account/idVerification, photo ID, usually minutes). Hand them the link and wait; `verificationStatus` DECLINED = contact support
- `SHARE_ACCESS_ENDED` - a site-share key reached the end of the time it was shared for; ask for it to be shared again
- `SHARE_NOT_FOUND` - a site-share link or code was already used, revoked, expired or mistyped; ask the person who shared it for a new one
- `NOT_SUPPORTED_FOR_PRODUCT` - wrong hosting product for this endpoint
- `PREVIEW_SITE_NOT_SUPPORTED` - free preview sites aren't API-managed
- `CLOUDFLARE_NOT_CONNECTED` - no active Cloudflare grant; the owner must authorize in a browser, then poll `/cloudflare/getConnection`
- `NOT_QUEUED` - that domain has never been queued for a Cloudflare move
- `TOO_MANY_DOMAINS` - more than 500 domains in one `/cloudflare/connect` call
- `CLOUDFLARE_REAUTHORIZE_REQUIRED` - the stored Cloudflare grant lacks the permission for that call; the owner reconnects at the returned `connectUrl`
- `FULL_ACCESS_ACKNOWLEDGMENT_REQUIRED` - admin role needs acknowledgeFullAccess
- `WP_CLI_FAILED` - the WordPress site rejected the command

- `INVALID_API_KEYS_001` - the public `apikey` is invalid/unknown
- `INVALID_API_KEYS_002` - the public key is valid but the `secretapikey` doesn't match
- `MISSING_SECRETAPIKEY` - no secret supplied (common cause: the field was named `secretkey` instead of `secretapikey`)
- `IP_NOT_ALLOWED` / `DOMAIN_NOT_ALLOWED` - request outside this key's allowlist
- `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_MISMATCH` / `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_IN_USE` - idempotency conflicts
- `SANDBOX_UNSUPPORTED` - this endpoint (hosting, email, closeouts) isn't simulated in the sandbox; use a live key
- `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` - HTTP 429; wait the seconds in the `Retry-After` header (also `ttlRemaining` / `X-RateLimit-Reset`)
  Every authenticated response carries `X-RateLimit-Limit` / `-Remaining` / `-Reset` / `-Window` for a general per-key request budget (20 per 2 seconds). While `X-RateLimit-Mode: observe` is present that budget is measured but **not** enforced, so exhausting it does not fail a request; per-operation limits still do.
- `MONTHLY_SPEND_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` - would exceed the account's monthly API spend limit (its own, or the $100 default); only the account holder can raise it
- `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` (HTTP 402) - `payWith: "usdc"` was sent: pay the `PAYMENT-REQUIRED` x402 terms and repeat the request with `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`; nothing was charged yet
- `PAYMENT_FAILED` (HTTP 402) - Coinbase refused the payment; nothing charged, fresh terms attached
- `PAYMENT_IN_PROGRESS` (HTTP 409) - another request is processing this payment; do not pay again
- `PAYMENT_PENDING` (HTTP 409) - the checkout named by `usdcCheckoutId` was paid and is settling; repeat after `retryAfter`, do not pay again
- `PAYMENT_MISMATCH` / `PAYMENT_NOT_FOUND` / `PAYMENT_ALREADY_USED` / `PAYMENT_EXPIRED` - `usdcCheckoutId` or `cardPaymentId` is for another purchase, unknown, already used (it bought something, or went to account credit after an hour unclaimed), or no longer payable; send the purchase without it for a new checkout
- `INSUFFICIENT_FUNDS` - not enough **prepaid account credit**; a purchase does not charge a saved card by itself, so having one is not enough on its own - `POST /account/topup` converts it into credit, with the user's OK. The response carries `cost`, `balance` and `shortfall` in cents, and **`topUpAvailable`**: `true` means a card is saved, so offer the user a top-up (with the amount; `topUpAmountToCover` is the minimum) and, with their OK, call `POST /account/topup` and retry the same request (`next_action.type` = `top_up`); `false` means no card: `POST /account/topupMpp` (the user's card through their agent wallet, MPP), `POST /account/topupCrypto` (USDC, an `x402Url` an agent's wallet can pay, or a `payUrl` for the person), or they add credit on the website (`add_funds`). If you do not charge cards on a user's behalf, treat `true` the same way: tell them the shortfall and let them add it. A short dry run reports the same fields
- `COST_MISMATCH` - `cost` must equal the current price in cents for the term being bought; the message names the expected value, and `dryRun` + `cost: 0` quotes it
- `DOMAIN_NOT_FOUND` / `INVALID_DOMAIN` - domain not in your account / invalid
- `DOMAIN_EXPIRED` - the domain has expired, so email on it can't be renewed until the domain is; nothing charged, renew the domain first
- `INVALID_TYPE` - unsupported DNS record type
- `CLOSEOUT_NOT_FOUND` / `CLOSEOUT_UNAVAILABLE` - not offered as a closeout / already claimed by another buyer
- `CLOSEOUT_NOT_ELIGIBLE` - the account is blocked from auctions/closeouts by support (past-due invoices or an auction terms violation); not retryable. There is no account-age or prior-order requirement - closeout eligibility is the same as registration plus verified email and phone
- `TRANSFER_INIT_FAILED` - the transfer could not be started and the order was refunded automatically; **not** a credentials or verification problem
- `TRANSFER_HOLD_NOT_AVAILABLE` - `holdForDnsSetup` unsupported for this TLD; nothing charged, resend without it
- `REGISTRANT_EMAIL_NOT_ACCEPTED` - the registry (currently .in and its second levels) refuses registrant contacts on temporary or encrypted email providers and suspends domains that use one; nothing was charged. Change the email on the account's default registrant contact and retry. This is about the contact on the domain, not about who hosts mail for it
- `TRANSFER_ZONE_EMPTY` - releasing would move the domain to an empty zone; import records first or pass `force: true`
- `TRANSFER_STATE_UNCONFIRMED` - the registry would not confirm the cancellation, so nothing was refunded and the transfer was left intact
- `DUPLICATE_RECORD` - that exact name/type/content already exists; nothing was created, and `existingId` holds the id of the record that does
- `RECORD_CONFLICT` - a CNAME cannot share a name with any other record type (RFC 1034); `conflictingRecords` lists what blocks it
- `NOTHING_TO_IMPORT` - `/dns/import` had nothing supplied and could discover nothing; if the domain already left its old registrar its records are unreadable and must be supplied explicitly
- `TOO_MANY_RECORDS` - more than 500 records in one `/dns/import` call
- `ZONE_RECORD_LIMIT` - the zone holds the maximum of 2,500 DNS records; nothing was created, `count` and `limit` give the current size and the ceiling, delete something first
- `SPF_CONFLICT` - this domain already has an apex SPF record and a second one is an RFC 7208 4.5 permerror that fails the check for every sender. Do NOT retry: edit the existing record instead. `existingId` and `existingContent` identify it, and when the two can be safely combined `suggestedMerge` is the exact record to write. Refused on create and on edit. An SPF record on a subdomain is unaffected - this is apex only
- `RESTORE_POINT_NOT_FOUND` - no such restore point for this domain; list them with `GET /dns/history/{domain}`. A point owned by another account reads identically rather than confirming it exists
- `RESTORE_POINT_EMPTY` - that restore point holds no records
- `DNS_READ_FAILED` - the live zone could not be read, so nothing was changed; retryable
- `BULK_CHECK_TOO_MANY` - more than 25 domains in one bulk check; nothing was checked, split the list
- `BULK_CHECK_TOO_SLOW` - the bulk batch's TLD mix needs too many sequential registry commands (.de is one domain per command); nothing was checked, split the slow TLDs out
- `DNSSEC_ALGORITHM_DEPRECATED` - this registry no longer accepts that DNSSEC algorithm or digest type (RFC 9904/9905/9906); the message names the value and a replacement. Affects create only, never read or delete
